name: Schezwan Noodles

ingredients.name: Refined sunflower oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2½ tsp (½ tsp for the boiled noodles + 2 tsp for the stir-fry)

ingredients.name: Spring onion (hara pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 stalks; whites and greens chopped separately

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium, cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: Schezwan chutney / Schezwan sauce (ready-made, e.g. Ching's Secret)
Salt, for the stir-fry
ingredients.householdMeasure: a small pinch, only if needed after tasting

equipment: Large pot or saucepan (at least 2 litres) for boiling the noodles
Wok or wide kadai (a heavy wide frying pan also works; cook on the highest heat and don't crowd it)
Two forks, tongs or chopsticks for tossing (a spatula plus a fork is fine)
Chopping board and a sharp knife
Measuring spoons (normal teaspoons and a tablespoon are fine stand-ins) and a plate

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Put 1 litre water and ¼ tsp salt in a large pot on high heat.
steps.tip: Plenty of water keeps the noodles from turning sticky.
steps.visualCue: Large, rolling bubbles across the whole surface.
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from a pot at a rolling boil.

steps.title: Measure the noodles
steps.text: Weigh out 75 g dry hakka noodles (half a 150 g packet).
steps.visualCue: About one and a half dry noodle bundles.
steps.cameraCheck: The dry noodles on a plate
steps.videoShot: Hands breaking a packet of noodles in half.

steps.title: Add the noodles
steps.text: Slide the noodles into the boiling water and loosen them gently with a fork.
steps.visualCue: The bundles separate and sink.
steps.videoShot: A fork loosening noodles in bubbling water.

steps.title: Cook until just done
steps.text: Boil on high heat, stirring once or twice, until the noodles are cooked but still firm (follow the packet time, usually 3–5 min).
steps.tip: Stop a minute early; the noodles cook again in the wok. Overcooked noodles break and turn mushy.
steps.visualCue: A strand pressed between fingers breaks cleanly with no hard white core and still has a slight bite.
steps.cameraCheck: One noodle strand pinched between two fingers
steps.videoShot: Tongs lifting a few strands out of the pot.

steps.title: Drain and rinse
steps.text: Tip the noodles into a colander and rinse under cold running water for 15–20 seconds.
steps.visualCue: The noodles feel cool and no longer steam.
steps.cameraCheck: The drained noodles in the colander
steps.videoShot: Cold water running over noodles in a colander.

steps.title: Oil the noodles
steps.text: Shake off the water and toss the noodles with ½ tsp oil. Spread them on a plate.
steps.visualCue: Glossy, loose strands that don't clump.
steps.cameraCheck: The oiled noodles spread on a plate
steps.videoShot: Fingers lifting shiny, separate noodles.

steps.title: Chop the garlic and ginger
steps.text: Finely chop 2 large garlic cloves (6 g) and ½ tsp ginger (2 g).
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even bits.
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped garlic and ginger on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife rocking over chopped garlic.

steps.title: Cut the spring onion
steps.text: Chop 2 spring onion stalks; keep the white parts and the green parts in separate heaps.
steps.visualCue: A small white heap and a larger green heap.
steps.cameraCheck: The two heaps on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing spring onion into rings.

steps.title: Slice the onion and capsicum
steps.text: Thinly slice 30 g onion (¼ medium) and 25 g capsicum (¼ medium).
steps.visualCue: Thin, even strips.
steps.videoShot: A knife cutting capsicum into thin strips.

steps.title: Cut the carrot
steps.text: Peel and cut 25 g carrot (¼ medium) into thin matchsticks.
steps.visualCue: Thin orange sticks about 4–5 cm long.
steps.videoShot: Knife cutting a carrot into fine strips.

steps.title: Shred the cabbage
steps.text: Finely shred 40 g cabbage (about ⅔ cup).
steps.visualCue: Thin, pale-green ribbons.
steps.videoShot: A knife shredding a cabbage wedge.

steps.title: Set out the sauces
steps.text: Put 1½ tbsp Schezwan chutney, 1 tsp soy sauce, ½ tsp vinegar and 1 tsp ketchup in a small bowl, next to the stove.
steps.tip: Taste your brand of Schezwan chutney first: brands vary a lot in heat and salt. If it is very hot, start with 1 tbsp.
steps.visualCue: A small bowl with a red paste and dark liquid.
steps.videoShot: Schezwan chutney spooned into a small bowl.

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Put the wok on the highest heat and add 2 tsp oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and the first wisp of smoke appears.
steps.cameraCheck: The hot oil in the wok
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling around a hot wok.

steps.title: Fry the garlic and ginger
steps.text: Add the chopped garlic and ginger and stir.
steps.tip: Don't let it brown dark; burnt garlic tastes bitter.
steps.visualCue: Sizzling, fragrant, just turning pale gold.
steps.videoShot: Garlic sizzling in oil.

steps.title: Add spring onion whites and onion
steps.text: Add the spring onion whites and the sliced onion; toss.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns glossy and just translucent at the edges but is still crunchy.
steps.videoShot: A spatula tossing onion slices.

steps.title: Add carrot and capsicum
steps.text: Add the carrot and capsicum; toss on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Colours brighten; the vegetables are still crisp.
steps.videoShot: Orange and green strips tossed in the wok.

steps.title: Add the cabbage
steps.text: Add the cabbage and toss.
steps.tip: Keep the heat high and keep moving; low heat makes the vegetables watery.
steps.visualCue: The cabbage wilts slightly but stays crunchy.
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed vegetables in the wok
steps.videoShot: Cabbage ribbons tossed with the other vegetables.

steps.title: Add the sauces
steps.text: Pour in the sauce bowl (Schezwan chutney, soy sauce, vinegar and ketchup) and stir for a few seconds.
steps.tip: Turn on the exhaust fan or open a window; the chilli fumes can make you cough.
steps.visualCue: The vegetables turn red and glossy; a sharp chilli-vinegar smell rises.
steps.videoShot: Red sauce sizzling as it hits the hot wok.

steps.title: Add the noodles
steps.text: Add the boiled noodles to the wok.
steps.visualCue: The noodles sit on top of the vegetables.
steps.videoShot: Noodles dropped onto the red vegetables.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Toss with two forks or tongs, lifting from the bottom, on high heat until every strand is coated.
steps.tip: Lift and toss rather than stir; stirring breaks the noodles.
steps.visualCue: Evenly red-orange noodles, hot throughout, with no pale patches.
steps.cameraCheck: A forkful of noodles lifted from the wok
steps.videoShot: Tongs lifting and tossing red noodles.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add a pinch of black pepper, taste and add a small pinch of salt only if needed. Toss once more.
steps.visualCue: Spicy, tangy and salty enough when tasted.
steps.videoShot: Pepper dusted over the noodles.

steps.title: Finish with spring onion greens
steps.text: Switch off the heat, add the spring onion greens and toss once.
steps.visualCue: Bright green flecks through the red noodles.
steps.cameraCheck: The finished noodles in the wok
steps.videoShot: Spring onion greens scattered over steaming noodles.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a plate and serve hot.
steps.visualCue: A heap of glossy, red, separate noodles with crunchy vegetables.
steps.videoShot: Noodles twirled onto a plate with a fork.

reasons: mostly refined-wheat (maida) noodles, so it digests fast with a high glycaemic response and only about 11 g protein, and the Schezwan chutney and soy sauce bring about 1,080 mg sodium (over half the day's limit). On the plus side it is stir-fried, not deep-fried, uses a measured 2½ tsp of unsaturated oil, and has about 135 g of vegetables, giving vitamin A, C and K and about 6 g fibre (est.). Restaurant versions use much more oil and sauce, often MSG, a larger portion and fewer vegetables, and are usually eaten with fried Manchurian.

researchRating.basis: a hugely popular Indo-Chinese street and restaurant dish across Mumbai and India, with recipes on every major Indian recipe site (Hebbar's Kitchen, Veg Recipes of India, Cook With Manali, Tarla Dalal, Spice Up The Curry, Yummy Tummy Aarthi) and listed by almost every Indo-Chinese outlet on the delivery apps; Hebbar's Kitchen's recipes are rated highly by readers. Deduction because it is widely seen as heavy, oily, salty junk food, and restaurant versions are often criticised as greasy or too spicy.

storage: Cool and refrigerate within 1 hour (cooked noodles, like rice, can grow Bacillus cereus if left warm). Fridge: up to 1–2 days in an airtight box; the vegetables lose their crunch. Freezer: not recommended (the noodles turn mushy and the vegetables watery). To reheat, sprinkle 1 tbsp water and toss in a hot pan for 2–3 min, or microwave covered for 1½–2 min, stirring halfway, until steaming hot throughout. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Schezwan noodle frankie. Warm a roti or paratha on a tawa, spread 1 tsp mint chutney or a little mayo, add a line of reheated Schezwan noodles, some sliced onion and shredded cabbage, roll it up tightly and toast seam-side down for 1 min. A Mumbai street-style wrap (Hebbar's Kitchen and Ranveer Brar both publish noodle frankies) that turns a soggy leftover into a crisp, hand-held snack.
burnOff: about 6.9 km of running (485 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 9.7 km of brisk walking (about 2 h at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With a side of Manchurian gravy (about +225 kcal), add about 3.2 km of running.

navratri.reason: wheat noodles, onion, garlic and table salt are all avoided on the common North and West Indian vrat rule set

ekadashi.reason: wheat (a grain) is the main ingredient, and grains are given up on Ekadashi

jain.reason: drop onion, spring onion, garlic, ginger and carrot and use a Jain (no onion, no garlic) Schezwan chutney; see the Jain variant

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so there is no halal concern; quick and filling for iftar, but salty (about 2.7 g salt) and very spicy, so it is a poor choice for sehri, when it can increase thirst during the fast

jain.reason: drop onion, spring onion, garlic, ginger and carrot (all roots or bulbs), and use a no-onion-no-garlic (Jain) Schezwan chutney instead of a regular one; see the Jain variant

vegan.reason: egg-free hakka noodles, oil, vegetables and plant sauces; no dairy, ghee, honey or egg (check the noodle pack: some "egg noodles" contain egg)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg, so it fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: drop onion, spring onion and garlic and use a no-onion-no-garlic Schezwan chutney; ginger can stay if your family allows it

glutenFree.reason: the noodles are refined wheat (maida), and soy sauce and most ready-made Schezwan chutneys contain wheat; a rice-noodle version is possible (see the Gluten-free variant)

dairyFree.reason: no milk, butter, ghee, cream or paneer in the main recipe

variants.name: Jain Schezwan Noodles (no onion, garlic or roots)

variants.reason: . Main recipe already vegan (egg-free noodles, oil, no dairy). Check that the noodle pack says egg-free.
